newsitem.title: FRANCE: GEC-Marconi ready to work with French state firms.
newsitem.headline: GEC-Marconi ready to work with French state firms.

text.p: General Electric Co's defence division, GEC-Marconi, is ready to work with French public sector companies, its chairman said in Paris on Wednesday.

Speaking after attending a hearing of the French parliament's defence committee, Sir Geoffrey Pattie said GEC-Marconi was ready to adapt to new situations. But he hoped France's new leftist government would take a quick decision on Thomson-CSF after halting its privatisation last week.

"We are waiting to see what the French government decides. We told the committee we are working with both public and private sector companies in France. It makes no difference. We will adapt," he told reporters after the session.

The right-wing opposition has attacked the recently elected Socialist-led governments' decision to scrap the privatisation planned by its predecessors, saying it would shut Thomson-CSF out of alliances with other big defence firms in Europe.
GEC-Marconi is one of the companies tipped to forge new links with a restructured Thomson-CSF, which is Europe's leading defence electronics supplier with a staff of 46,000.
Pattie said that because of the rapid concentration of defence industries in the United States it was important for France to make a new decision on Thomson-CSF "very rapidly".
He was ready to meet French government officials at any time to discuss the case.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's office, which is handling the sensitive privatisation issue, said on Friday it would soon issue new guidelines for Thomson-CSF that would involve a "decisive" public shareholding in a French defence giant.
